items.headline: 69 arrested under Arunachal anti-terror law
items.text: Police say 69 people have been arrested and four detained under Arunachal's Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act over the 23 October arson in Pasighat, in 55 cases. A minister met representatives of 72 villages on the dam and said local communities' rights must stay central.

photo.alt: A wide river with sandbanks and a long bridge, seen between forested hills, under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: The Siang river near Pasighat, where curbs on gatherings remain after the 23 October violence.

items.headline: Karnataka voter roll shrinks by nearly one crore
items.text: Karnataka's final voter roll, published on 27 October after a special revision, lists about 4.55 crore electors, nearly one crore fewer than before; Bengaluru's fell from about 1.03 crore to 59.08 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer says deletion forms covered electors found ineligible at hearings, and denies bulk filings without reasons.

photo.alt: Men, women and children stand in a queue on the veranda of an old school building used as a polling booth.
photo.caption: Voters queue at a polling booth in Bengaluru during the 2014 general election.

items.headline: Dalit man killed; wife's brother arrested
items.text: Akshay, a 23-year-old Dalit man who married against his wife's family's wishes, was beaten with bricks in Khatauli on Monday and died on Tuesday. Police arrested two people on Wednesday, including her brother, and say the killing appears premeditated.

items.headline: Foreign nationality alone no bar to UAPA bail
items.text: The Supreme Court ruled on 27 October that the UAPA's bail bar for foreigners applies only if the prosecution shows the accused entered India illegally, dismissing the Union government's appeal against bail for a Sri Lankan national.

items.headline: UN warns Kordofan sieges risk new atrocities
items.text: A year after the RSF seized El Fasher, UN officials warned on Wednesday that sieges in Kordofan and Blue Nile could bring new atrocities; UN investigators said they found hallmarks of genocide in El Fasher. No army or RSF response was reported; the RSF says El Fasher is safe for civilians.

photo.alt: A loaded lorry with people sitting on top drives along a road shaded by large trees.
photo.caption: A road in Bara, North Kordofan, one of the regions where UN officials warn sieges could bring new atrocities.

items.place: Rafah and Khan Younis, Gaza Strip
items.headline: Five killed in Gaza strikes after Israeli vote
items.text: Israeli strikes in Rafah and Khan Younis killed five people on Wednesday, Gaza's civil defence agency and a hospital said, three of them in a drone strike in Rafah. The Israeli army said it 'struck terrorists in the area'.

photo.alt: A dirt road between collapsed and badly damaged multi-storey buildings and piles of rubble.
photo.caption: Destroyed buildings in Gaza City's Sheikh Radwan district in 2025. Wednesday's strikes hit Rafah and Khan Younis.

items.headline: Hebron operation now affects about 5,000 people
items.text: About 780 families, roughly 5,000 people, have been displaced or are trapped at home as Israel's Hebron operation entered its sixth day, the city's municipality says. The army began it after two soldiers were killed on Friday; no Israeli comment on the figures was reported.

items.headline: Egypt court orders Mada Masr shut
items.text: A Cairo court ordered the independent outlet Mada Masr closed and fined editor Lina Attalah 3 million Egyptian pounds for running an unlicensed website. She was held for hours until the fine was paid and faces a retrial on 11 November over a 2024 sentence. No official comment was reported.

items.headline: Tear gas at Jakarta protest over graft, fires
items.text: Thousands protested in Jakarta and four other cities on Wednesday over corruption and the handling of wildfires, seeking a national emergency. Police fired tear gas in Jakarta after bottles were thrown. The government said it understands the students' concerns.

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. After arson in Pasighat on 23 October, police say 69 people have been arrested under the state's anti-terror law; curbs on gatherings continue, and two activists in custody are reportedly on hunger strike.
focus.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
